text.textPath: The dawn city bus runs with its windows decked i
n some dazzling finery. The harsher the dead of winter, the m
ore vividly the frost flowers bloom. Those who rode this bus yesterday maid
ens and bachelors, children and grown-ups, hairdressers, salesmen, housemaids, the jobless t
heir breath and their sighs met in secret overnight and brought forth this fla
shing, breathtaking beauty. As if I had wandered into some exhibition, I move from seat to sea
t to look, and once again I am drunk on a single petal, on its delicate and cold beauty. Whose desolate sigh was th
is? What warm heart breathed out this breath of passion? For no reason, carefully, with my breath and my finger, I wipe away a single frost
petal and press my forehead to the glass. A haggard face glimmers in the rattling window friend, you walked the r
oad beside me for so long, and now I am not even allowed to visit you. The dawn city bus runs with its windows decked in some dazzling fi
nery. The harsher the dead of winter, the more vividly the frost flowers bloom. Those who rode this bus yesterday maidens and bachelors, children and grown-ups, hairdr
